## Left open by the earlier read (RD-126)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule L08 (Major). Problem: This lesson is designated as Filipino, but its teaching prose is in English. Teach the concepts in simple Filipino at the Grade 5 standard.
   > **Citizenship** means legal membership in a country. Some rights and public offices depend on it.
2. Rule L10 (Major). Problem: All eleven examples have English questions and solutions. This lesson is designated as Filipino, so its examples must be in Filipino.
   > A child born in $2005$ has a Filipino mother and an alien father. Is the child Filipino from birth?
3. Rule L12 (Minor). Problem: The teaching prose uses full English explanations in a lesson designated as Filipino. Use Filipino teaching prose and retain English only where it is the common term.
   > **Suffrage** is the right to vote. Article V, Section $1$ requires Philippine citizenship, age of at least $18$, and no legal disqualification.
4. Rule L22a (Minor). Problem: This paragraph has four sentences. L22a limits each paragraph to one to three short sentences. Split the definition and covered groups from the procedural conditions.
   > **Repatriation** restores former Philippine citizenship. RA $8171$ covers Filipino women who lost citizenship through marriage to aliens. It also covers natural-born Filipinos who lost it from political or economic necessity, including their minor children. Restrictions apply; an oath and registration with the proper civil registry and Bureau of Immigration are required.
5. Rule L25 (Major). Problem: The required oath of allegiance is never explained. A student must know that this means a formal sworn promise of loyalty to understand the reacquisition step used again in example 6. No prerequisite teaching or later explanation is supplied.
   > Those who lost citizenship through foreign naturalization reacquire it through the prescribed oath of allegiance to the Philippines.
6. Rule L25 (Major). Problem: Certificate of candidacy is a necessary legal term for the filing deadline, but the lesson never explains that it is the formal document filed to run for an elective office. Example 6 repeats the term without teaching it.
   > Under Section $5(2)$, seeking elected office also requires a personal, sworn renunciation of all foreign citizenship when filing the certificate of candidacy.
